topic.name: Finding the Area of a Polar Region

question.text: Find the area bounded by the polar curve $r = 3e^{2\theta}$ for $0 \leq \theta \leq \pi.$
question.explanation:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by \[ A = \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} r^2(\theta) \textrm{d}\theta \,. \]

When $r(\theta) = 3e^{2\theta}$, $\theta_1=0$ and $\theta_2= \pi$, this gives

\begin{align*} A &= \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} r^2 \:\textrm{d}\theta\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{\pi} \left( 3e^{2\theta} \right)^2 \:\textrm{d}\theta\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9}{2} \int_{0}^{\pi} e^{4\theta} \:\textrm{d}\theta\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{4} e^{4\theta} \, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9}{8} \left( e^{4\pi} - e^{0} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9}{8} \left( e^{4\pi} - 1 \right). \end{align*}

example.title: Finding Areas Bounded by Other Polar Curves

question.text: Which of the following gives the total area enclosed by the graph of the polar curve $r = 1+\dfrac{\sin(\theta)}{3}$ for $\dfrac{\pi}{2} \leq \theta \leq {\pi}?$
question.explanation:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by \[ A = \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} r^2(\theta) \textrm{d}\theta \,. \]

When $r(\theta) = 1+\dfrac{\sin(\theta)}{3}$, $\theta_1=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\theta_2={\pi}$, this gives

\[ A = \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}\left(1+\dfrac{\sin(\theta)}{3}\right)^2 \textrm{d}\theta \,. \]

question.text: Find the area bounded by the polar curve $r = 2 - \sin\theta$ for $0 \leq \theta \leq \pi,$ as shown above.
question.explanation:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by \[ A = \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} r^2(\theta) \textrm{d}\theta \,. \]

When $r(\theta) = 2 - \sin\theta$, $\theta_1=0$ and $\theta_2={\pi}$, this gives

\begin{align*} A &= \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} r^2 \:\textrm{d}\theta \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{\pi} (2 - \sin\theta)^2 \:\textrm{d}\theta \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{\pi} (4- 4\sin\theta + \sin^2\theta) \:\textrm{d}\theta \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \left( 4\theta \, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} +4\cos\theta \, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} + \dfrac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi} (1-\cos(2\theta))\:\textrm{d}\theta \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \left( 4\theta \, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} +4\cos\theta \, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} + \dfrac{1}{2}\left( \theta \, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} - \dfrac{\sin(2\theta)}{2}\, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} \right)\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \left( 4\theta \, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} +4\cos\theta \, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} + \dfrac{1}{2}\theta \, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} - \dfrac{\sin(2\theta)}{4} \, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9}{4}\theta \, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} + 2\cos\theta \, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} - \dfrac{\sin(2\theta)}{8} \, \Biggr|_{0}^{\pi} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9}{4}\left(\pi - 0\right) + 2\left(\cos\left({\pi}\right)-\cos\left(0\right)\right) - \dfrac{1}{8} \left(\sin\left({2\pi}\right) - \sin\left(0\right)\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9\pi}{4} + 2(-2) - \dfrac{1}{8}(0) \\[5pt] % &= \dfrac{3\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9\pi-16}{4}. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Area Bounded by the Loop of a Limaçon

question.text: Find the area bounded by the polar curve $r = 2- 2\sin\theta$ for $\dfrac{\pi}{2} \leq \theta \leq \pi.$
question.explanation:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by \[ A = \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} r^2(\theta) \textrm{d}\theta \,. \]

When $r(\theta) = 2 - 2\sin\theta$, $\theta_1=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\theta_2={\pi}$, this gives

\begin{align*} A &= \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} r^2 \:\textrm{d}\theta \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\pi/2}^{\pi} (2 - 2\sin\theta)^2 \:\textrm{d}\theta \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\pi/2}^{\pi} (4- 8\sin\theta + 4\sin^2\theta) \:\textrm{d}\theta \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \left( 4\theta \, \Biggr|_{\pi/2}^{\pi} +8\cos\theta \, \Biggr|_{\pi/2}^{\pi} -2\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi} (-1+\cos(2\theta))\:\textrm{d}\theta \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \left( 4\theta \, \Biggr|_{\pi/2}^{\pi} +8\cos\theta \, \Biggr|_{\pi/2}^{\pi} -2\left( -\theta \, \Biggr|_{\pi/2}^{\pi} + \dfrac{\sin(2\theta)}{2}\, \Biggr|_{\pi/2}^{\pi} \right)\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \left( 4\theta \, \Biggr|_{\pi/2}^{\pi} +8\cos\theta \, \Biggr|_{\pi/2}^{\pi} + 2\theta \, \Biggr|_{\pi/2}^{\pi} - \sin(2\theta) \, \Biggr|_{\pi/2}^{\pi} \right) \\[5pt] &=3\theta \, \Biggr|_{\pi/2}^{\pi} + 4\cos\theta \, \Biggr|_{\pi/2}^{\pi} - \dfrac{\sin(2\theta)}{2} \, \Biggr|_{\pi/2}^{\pi} \\[5pt] &= 3\left(\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + 4\left(\cos\left({\pi}\right)-\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right) - \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\sin\left({2\pi}\right) - \sin\left(\pi\right)\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3\pi}{2} + 4\cdot (-1) - \dfrac{1}{2}(0) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3\pi}{2}- 4 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3\pi-8}{2}. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Area Bounded by the Loop of a Limaçon

question.text: Find the area $A$ bounded by the polar curve $r = 2e^{\theta}$ for $0 \leq \theta \leq \ln(2),$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by \[ A = \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} r^2(\theta)\,\textrm{d}\theta. \]

When $r(\theta) = 2e^{\theta}$, $\theta_1=0$ and $\theta_2=\ln(2)$, this gives

\begin{align*} A &= \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} r^2 \:\textrm{d}\theta \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{\ln(2)} (2e^{\theta})^2 \:\textrm{d}\theta \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{\ln(2)} 4e^{2\theta} \:\textrm{d}\theta \\[5pt] &= 2 \int_{0}^{\ln(2)} e^{2\theta} \:\textrm{d}\theta \\[5pt] &= 2 \left(\dfrac{e^{2\theta}}{2}\right)\Biggr|_{0}^{\ln(2)} \\[5pt] &= e^{2\theta}\,\Biggr|_{0}^{\ln(2)} \\[5pt] &= e^{2\ln(2)} - e^{0} \\[5pt] &= 4 - 1 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{3}. \end{align*}
